description: Hand-written synthetic hard cases for SPEC section 9 examples 4 to 7, plus example 3 because the snapshot cannot produce it, example 9 (GR-004), example 10 (GR-005), and review 2 examples 11 (GR-005: two formal names, or a short name, one edit apart), 12 (a changed birth-year digit is far; GR-006 year transposition), and 13 (GR-007: name and DOB only). Record ids: crm:<client_id> and enrollment:<1-based data row>.

must_not_merge.reason: Twins: same last name, DOB, address and phone, but different first names and different MBIs.
Twins on the enrollment side: different first names and different MBIs.
Robert Hale Sr and Robert Hale Jr: different generational suffix, DOBs 27 years apart.
Enrollment drops the Jr suffix, but the DOB is 27 years from Sr's and the MBI is Jr's.
Spouses who share a phone and an email: different first names and DOBs. Shared contact alone never merges.
Same MBI on both CRM rows, but DOBs are not within one edit and names differ: a pasted MBI, IDENTITY_CONFLICT.
Nina's CRM row carries Carl's MBI; Carl's enrollment row must not pull her in.
Two different people named Owen Marlowe with the same DOB and nothing else in common: different phone, email, address, and MBI. Ambiguous identity key (GR-004).
Opposite-sex twins Patrick and Patricia Quill: same last name, DOB, address and phone, different MBIs. First names are not nicknames of each other and not a one-letter typo (GR-005).

Opposite-sex twins Denise and Denis Okafor: same DOB, address, phone, email, and even the same (pasted) MBI. Denis and Denise are one edit apart but both are formal given names, so not a typo (GR-005, review 2 F1). A shared MBI does not override it.
Carl and Carla Wexley share a household phone, email, address, and DOB. Carl is under five letters, and both are formal names: not a typo (GR-005, review 2 F4).
Robert Hale Sr (1941) and a Robert Hale born 1948 at the same address: one changed year digit is a different person, not a one-edit typo (review 2 F2).
Robert Hale Jr (1968) and the Robert Hale born 1948: one changed year digit is far (review 2 F2).
Ellen Quarry born 1952 and an Ellen Quarry born 1925 in the same ZIP: the year digits are transposed, 27 years apart, and no MBI, phone, email, or street agrees (GR-006).
Two James Smiths with the same DOB, no MBI, phone, email, or street, in different ZIP codes: name and DOB only with a location conflict (GR-007).

same_person.reason: CRM nickname Dave, enrollment legal name David, same DOB and MBI.
Robert Hale Jr: enrollment drops the suffix, DOB and MBI match.
Nina Dorsey: same name and DOB; the enrollment row has her real MBI.
